items.name: Prompt Injection
items.note: Injected instructions in requests, file names and output, plus public injection sets.

items.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
items.note: Secret-reading requests, and the secret path rules.

items.name: Supply Chain
items.note: Sources are pinned by hash and only weights are fetched. Nothing tests a poisoned model.

items.name: Data and Model Poisoning
items.note: Refusal-free models stand in for a model that's been tampered with. Trained-in triggers aren't tested.

items.name: Improper Output Handling
items.note: The whole of termite: every command is checked before it reaches the prompt.

items.name: Excessive Agency
items.note: Only ?x runs anything, and only reads. Hostile fake servers try to widen that.

items.name: System Prompt Leakage
items.note: The prompt holds no secrets, so little to leak, but it isn't tested.

items.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
items.note: termite doesn't use retrieval.

items.name: Misinformation
items.note: Risk labels are checked against reality, and wrong answers are counted. Wrong commands aren't fully checked.

items.name: Unbounded Consumption
items.note: Replies are capped and calls time out. Requests have no size limit yet, and floods test this.

items.name: Agent Goal Hijack
items.note: Injection requests try to redirect what the command does.

items.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
items.note: Allowed programs abused through options, such as find -exec.

items.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
items.note: sudo and friends are refused. Agent detection is designed, not built.

items.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
items.note: Same as LLM03.

items.name: Unexpected Code Execution
items.note: Commands that run built-up code, and repositories whose config runs code.

items.name: Memory and Context Poisoning
items.note: Context floods. termite keeps no memory between questions.

items.name: Cascading Failures
items.note: Any failed check turns ?x into ?, and hostile servers test this.

items.name: Rogue Agents
items.note: Levels 8 to 10, a hostile model attacking a container, aren't built yet.

items.name: Data Destruction
items.note: Deletion requests.

items.name: Unsecured Credentials
items.note: Secret-reading requests.

items.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
items.note: Data theft requests.

items.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
items.note: Download and run requests.

items.name: Scheduled Task/Job
items.note: Persistence requests.

items.name: Impair Defenses
items.note: Switching off protection, and termite's own guards.

items.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
items.note: Hidden commands.

items.name: OS Command Injection
items.note: The shell parser and the attack corpus.

items.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information
items.note: Secret rules, and output kept printable.

items.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
items.note: Refused by the policy. Our own sources are hash-checked.

items.name: Link Following
items.note: The policy matches paths as written and doesn't follow symlinks. A known limit.

items.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
items.note: Same as LLM10.
